newsitem.title: ESTONIA: UNION BANK LAUNCHES FIRST INDEX FUND.
newsitem.headline: UNION BANK LAUNCHES FIRST INDEX FUND.

text.p: Estonia's Union Bank said on Friday it has launched the country's first share index fund which is based on the 12 leading stocks on the Tallinn Stock Exchange.
The bank's vice president Margus Schults said the fund was a joint venture between Union Bank and Swedish company Dagens Industri that owns Estonia's daily business newspaper, Aripaev.
Union Bank holds a 51 percent interest and Dagens Industri 49 percent with the joint management vehicle called Uhishalduse AB. Sales started on Friday.
Schults said all companies included in the fund have market capitalisation of 100 million kroons and are considered to have sufficient liquidity.
He said the fund would be expanded to cover 15 companies by the middle of 1997, including Estonian Gas, Estonian Metals Export Co (EMEX) and media company Levico.
"This is the first and only such fund in Estonia and we hope it will attract foreign interest," Schults told Reuters.
"Through the fund investors can spread any risk over the economy rather than in just one stock,"
The fund is based on the Aripaev (AP) index that was set up in April 1995.
The index started at 100 and now stands at 669.
Shares in the AP index fund are sold according to the level of the index with one share costing 6.69 kroons at current levels.
